# Gate Requirements Checklist: The gate lints again, and it is one command

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the requirements for restoring lint to this package's gate and giving the gate's command list one home — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability and coverage — before any code is written.
**Created**: 2026-11-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the claim that nothing lints this package stated as measured evidence rather than an impression? [Completeness, Spec § Overview] — three measurements on `develop@2128be6`: no config file, no dependency in any of the three dependency maps, no lint step among the `checks` job's six commands.
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec establish that the omission was accidental rather than a decision, so this is not undoing someone's choice? [Completeness, Spec § Overview] — it does, and from the originating pull request's own evidence block, which quotes six commands where the source's chain ran seven. No ADR, `CLAUDE.md` passage or CHANGELOG entry says otherwise.
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements stated for what happens to findings the lint raises, not only for making it run? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002] — FR-002 requires each fixed in code, and bounds when a rule may be relaxed instead.
- [x] CHK004 Are the directories that must be excluded named, rather than left as "generated files"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003] — `specs/`, `.agents/`, `.specify/` and scratch output, with `__tests__/` and fixtures handled as config entries rather than exclusions.
- [x] CHK005 Is a requirement stated for the drift that let the step vanish, not only for the missing step? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005] — FR-004 gives the chain one home and FR-005 makes the workflow call it, with a test.
- [x] CHK006 Are the documents that must change enumerated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008] — `CLAUDE.md` § Coding standards, `CLAUDE.md` § CI and `docs/testing.md`.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "ESLint runs over this repo's source" specific about where its configuration comes from? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001] — the shared `@chrisgriffin/config` ESLint base; the plan adds that the source's own config file is the starting point and why.
- [x] CHK008 Is the boundary between "fix the code" and "relax the rule" drawn clearly enough that a builder cannot relax its way to green? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002] — a relaxation needs a comment naming what in this codebase makes the rule inapplicable, and is never for a real defect.
- [x] CHK009 Is it clear what `verify` contains, as against what `checks` contains? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Plan § Technical context] — `checks` is the chain, `verify` is `checks` plus the suite; the plan gives both as scripts.
- [x] CHK010 Is "one home for the command list" specific about which file that is? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004] — `package.json`.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Do FR-004 and FR-006 conflict — one asks for a single command, the other forbids CI from using it? [Conflict, Spec §FR-004, §FR-006] — resolved, and the resolution is explicit in both the spec and the plan: `verify` is the local gate; CI calls `checks` and keeps the suite as its own job, because a `checks` job running `verify` would bill the suite twice per pull request.
- [x] CHK012 Does the requirement to collapse the docs' command lists agree with `CLAUDE.md`'s own rule about a list stated in more than one doc? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008] — it is that rule applied; the plan says so.
- [x] CHK013 Is the count of commands in the current chain stated consistently? [Consistency] — six on `develop`, against the source's seven, in the overview, the plan and T001.
- [x] CHK014 Does FR-003's handling of `__tests__/` agree with the plan's config overrides? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Plan] — both say Node and Jest globals as a config entry, not an exclusion.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK015 Is exactly one success criterion marked as the runnable line, and does it fail on today's tree? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — one, run this pass: exit 1, `eslint is not a dependency`.
- [x] CHK016 Does the runnable line prove the lint passes, not merely that it is installed? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — it chains `npx eslint .` after the dependency check, so a configured but failing lint still exits non-zero.
- [x] CHK017 Is the anti-drift requirement checkable rather than asserted? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria, Tasks §T012] — the criterion asks for a deliberate break and its output; T012 specifies breaking `ci.yml`, seeing the test fail, and reverting.
- [x] CHK018 Can "the suite runs in exactly one CI job" be verified by a reviewer? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria, Tasks §T013] — the criterion requires naming every job a pull request runs and what each runs.
- [x] CHK019 Can "no registry token" be verified, rather than reasoned about? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria, Tasks §T003] — T003 runs `npm ci` in a shell with no credential configured and quotes the result.
- [x] CHK020 Is the `CLAUDE.md` size constraint expressed as a number a reviewer can check? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — 9500 bytes, the budget that file's own `checks` job enforces.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for the contributor running the gate locally? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios] — scenario 1, which is also why `verify` exists.
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for a fork contributor, who has no credentials? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios, §FR-007] — scenario 2 and FR-007, with T003 proving it.
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for the next person who adds a step to the gate? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios, §FR-005] — scenario 3, and the pin that makes it hold.
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for the reader of `CLAUDE.md` whose claim about ESLint is currently false? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios, §FR-008] — scenario 4 and FR-008.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK025 Does the spec say what happens if the lint raises a finding that is a genuine defect the suite does not cover? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-002, Tasks §T006] — FR-002 and T006: fixed in the code, never relaxed away, and listed in the pull request. T005 calls that set "the real baseline" precisely because the suite is green.
- [x] CHK026 Does the spec say what happens if fixing a finding changes behaviour? [Gap, Edge Case, Tasks §T007] — T007 pins the suite's counts at 71 / 2096 / 1 and says a changed count must be stated, not accepted.
- [x] CHK027 Is the case of an unexpected `.prettierignore` entry covered, given `CLAUDE.md` ties that file to `docs/testing.md`? [Coverage, Plan § Surfaces touched, Tasks §T021] — T021 covers both halves of that coupling.
- [x] CHK028 Does the spec bound how far the lint's strictness may go, so "restore" cannot become "raise the bar"? [Coverage, Spec § Out of scope] — the out-of-scope section forbids any rule beyond the shared base and the source's own config.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK029 Is the cost of the change stated, including the cost deliberately avoided? [Completeness, Plan § Surfaces touched] — the `cost` line: nothing added, and FR-006 exists to stop `verify` doubling the suite's minute per pull request.
- [x] CHK030 Are the required check names addressed, so a reader knows no branch ruleset edit is owed? [Coverage, Spec § Out of scope, Plan § Surfaces touched] — both say no job is added, removed or renamed. This matters more here than usually: `CLAUDE.md` makes a ruleset edit land _before_ a check is renamed or gated.
- [x] CHK031 Is the published surface addressed, given this is a released package? [Coverage, Plan § Surfaces touched] — `files`, `bin` and `exports` are untouched, and `check-package.sh` confirms it from inside the chain.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK032 Are the dependencies this adds named, with their source? [Dependency, Spec §FR-001, Plan] — `eslint`, `globals` and `@chrisgriffin/config` from `github:chrisgriffin/config#v1`.
- [x] CHK033 Is the assumption that a `github:` dependency needs no credential stated and given a check, rather than assumed? [Assumption, Plan § Technical context, Tasks §T003] — the plan flags it as the one point to verify deliberately, and T003 verifies it.
- [x] CHK034 Is the assumption documented that the source's own ESLint config is the right starting point? [Assumption, Plan § Technical context] — with its reason: the config already encodes why each override exists, and rewriting it would mean rediscovering each finding.
- [x] CHK035 Is it stated that the release tooling owns `CHANGELOG.md` and `version`, so neither is edited here? [Assumption, Plan § Surfaces touched] — it is, citing `CLAUDE.md`'s ban on hand-bumping.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK036 Is the scope of "one command" unambiguous — does `verify` include the suite or not? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004] — it does, and FR-006 then keeps CI off it. Both halves are stated rather than left to the reader.
- [ ] CHK037 Does the spec resolve whether the missing `coverage` script belongs in this change? [Ambiguity, Spec § Out of scope] — **left open, deliberately.** The out-of-scope section settles it for this ticket, and the reason is honest: what a coverage gate should assert here is not decided, and guessing would invent a standard. Open because that decision is genuinely outstanding, not because the spec is wrong.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
